stories.title: Rich Development Trades Newly Built Shopping Center
stories.excerpt: Hanley Investment Group Real Estate Advisors recently arranged the sale of Apple Valley Towne Center, a newly built 87,042-square-foot regional shopping center located at 19390 Bear Valley Rd. in Apple Valley. The center is 100% occupied by three national junior box tenants, Hobby Lobby, Marshalls and Five Below, and is shadow anchored by Stater Bros. Markets, Lowe’s Home Improvement and Walgreens. EVPs Kevin Fryman and Bill Asher, along with SVP Sean Cox, represented the seller and developer, Rich Development Enterprises of San Pedro. The buyer and purchase price were not disclosed. “We listed the property before the tenants opened for business, which gave the center early exposure and generated strong interest from private, mid-market and institutional investors,” said Fryman. “Presenting the assets both individually and as a three-tenant package expanded the buyer pool.” Completed in 2026, Apple Valley Towne Center features new long-term triple-net leases with scheduled rental increases every five years. The post Rich Development Trades Newly Built Shopping Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Rich Development sold newly built 87,042-sf Apple Valley Towne Center, 100% leased to Hobby Lobby, Marshalls, Five Below.
Property completed 2026 with triple-net leases featuring 5-year rent escalations; strong investor demand reported.
Apple Valley, CA retail center; minimal direct multifamily relevance.
stories.summary: Rich Development Enterprises sold Apple Valley Towne Center, a newly completed 87,042-square-foot regional shopping center in Apple Valley, CA, fully leased to three national tenants. The property features long-term triple-net leases with scheduled rent increases every five years. Hanley Investment Group brokered the deal, noting strong interest from private, mid-market, and institutional buyers.
stories.impact: Limited direct impact on multifamily development. Retail asset class dynamics and institutional appetite for recently built, fully leased properties signal capital availability and lender confidence in 2026 completions, but this does not inform apartment demand or supply signals in any specific metro.

stories.title: Doug Middleton to Lead New York Institutional Capital Markets at Cushman & Wakefield
stories.excerpt: Cushman & Wakefield has hired Doug Middleton and Jack Stillwagon to lead its Institutional Capital Markets business across New York City. Joining from CBRE, Middleton and Stillwagon bring extensive experience in sourcing and executing transactions for large commercial assets across New York City. At Cushman & Wakefield, they will also collaborate with capital markets teams across the country. Middleton joins the firm as executive vice chairman. For the past eight years, he led CBRE’s Investment Properties Institutional Group in New York City, following his role as director of investment sales at Eastdil Secured. Over the course of his career, Middleton has spearheaded billions of dollars in transactions citywide. Stillwagon joins as executive managing director. At CBRE, he worked alongside Middleton, advising on deals across the office, residential and industrial sectors and was actively involved in all phases of the transaction process. Mr. Stillwagon previously held positions at Waterfall Properties and Atlantic Creek Real Estate Partners. The post Doug Middleton to Lead New York Institutional Capital Markets at Cushman & Wakefield appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Cushman & Wakefield hired Doug Middleton (ex-CBRE EVP) and Jack Stillwagon as NYC institutional capital markets leads.
Middleton led $8M-plus transactions over career at CBRE Investment Properties and Eastdial Secured.
Leadership hire signals active NYC institutional deal flow; no direct demand or supply change.
stories.summary: Cushman & Wakefield hired Doug Middleton as executive vice chairman and Jack Stillwagon as executive managing director to lead its institutional capital markets business in New York City. Both were formerly at CBRE, where Middleton directed the Investment Properties Institutional Group for eight years and managed billions in transactions across office, residential, and industrial sectors.
stories.impact: Personnel moves at major brokerages reflect confidence in transaction volume and capital deployment in NYC, but signal no new demand, supply, or cost drivers affecting multifamily development. Useful as a proxy for CRE market momentum in Manhattan, but no second-order effect on apartment fundamentals.

stories.title: Gilbane, Strada Development Break Ground on Affordable Tower in Castle Hill/Soundview
stories.excerpt: City and state officials joined Gilbane, Strada Development LLC and the Center for Urban Community Services (CUCS) to break ground on 1920 Turnbull, a $175-million affordable and supportive housing development located at 1920 Turnbull Ave. in the Castle Hill/Soundview neighborhood of the Bronx. 1920 Turnbull will deliver a 22-story building with 228 affordable rental apartments, including 137 permanent supportive housing units for formerly homeless individuals and families. The community will also include a 24/7 staffed lobby, outdoor recreation space, a fitness room, community room, bike storage, laundry facilities and other resident-focused amenities. CUCS will operate a 3,500-square-foot onsite office space. Completion is anticipated in March 2029. 1920 Turnbull is the first of two planned buildings, with Phase 2 set to add 207 additional affordable apartments, 18% of which will be supportive housing. Construction is planned to begin within the next year, pending city approvals The post Gilbane, Strada Development Break Ground on Affordable Tower in Castle Hill/Soundview appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Gilbane and Strada Development broke ground on $175M affordable tower in Bronx's Castle Hill/Soundview, 228 units.
1920 Turnbull: 22-story, 137 supportive housing units for formerly homeless; Phase 2 planned 207 units within one year.
Completion March 2029; CUCS onsite operations signal mission-driven, public-subsidy-backed development.
stories.summary: Gilbane and Strada Development broke ground on 1920 Turnbull, a $175 million affordable and supportive housing development at 1920 Turnbull Ave. in the Bronx's Castle Hill/Soundview neighborhood. Phase 1 delivers 228 apartments across 22 stories, including 137 permanent supportive housing units for formerly homeless individuals; Phase 2 will add 207 units. Completion is anticipated in March 2029.
stories.impact: Demonstrates continued public investment and subsidy availability for affordable housing in outer-borough NYC submarkets, but signals limited rent-paying demand and lower-margin development economics. The pipeline of 435+ deeply affordable units in Bronx indicates supply growth that will not compete with market-rate multifamily; however, success of public-supported models may constrain land costs and financing appetite for market-rate development in Castle Hill/Soundview over the next 3–4 years.

stories.title: Private Event Space Planned to Top Former Hancock Center
stories.excerpt: 360 CHICAGO, the 94th-floor observation deck atop 875 North Michigan Avenue (the former John Hancock Center), announced that its new private event venue, planned for the 96th floor of the building, will begin accepting bookings in 2027.Spanning nearly 14,000 square feet and more than 1,000 feet above the city, ELEVAIRE CHICAGO will pair sweeping views of Lake Michigan and the city’s skyline with customizable spaces. The opening of the new 96th-floor private event space is part of a major expansion of 360 CHICAGO into the 95th and 96th floors of 875 North Michigan Avenue. The expansion will ultimately increase 360 CHICAGO’s footprint to more than 50,000 square feet across three floors and create Chicago’s first multi-story observation deck.360 CHICAGO announced plans to expand into the 95th and 96th floors in 2025 after its parent company, Magnicity, acquired the two floors the previous year. Magnicity has brought on Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM), the original architects and engineers of 875 North Michigan Avenue, to lead the design of the new floors. The post Private Event Space Planned to Top Former Hancock Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: 875 North Michigan Avenue (ex-Hancock Center) adding 96th-floor private event venue ELEVAIRE CHICAGO, 14,000 sq ft.
Bookings begin 2027; part of major expansion into 95th and 96th floors of iconic downtown Chicago tower.
Office/hospitality conversion play; no multifamily relevance.
stories.summary: 360 CHICAGO announced that ELEVAIRE CHICAGO, a new 14,000-square-foot private event venue on the 96th floor of 875 North Michigan Avenue, will begin accepting bookings in 2027. The venue is part of a broader expansion of 360 CHICAGO into the 95th and 96th floors of the former John Hancock Center and will offer customizable event spaces with panoramic views.
stories.impact: No material impact on multifamily development. This is a hospitality/observation deck capital investment in downtown Chicago's core, reflecting hotel and experiential venue demand, but does not signal population migration, employment growth, or rental demand that would inform apartment development underwriting in any Chicago submarket.

stories.title: PCCP Provides $41M Refi on North Park Multifamily
stories.excerpt: PCCP has provided a $41-million senior loan to refinance Tenney North Park, a newly constructed, 125-unit multifamily property with ground-floor retail in San Diego’s North Park submarket. The loan was provided on behalf of owner and developer Foulger-Pratt and refinanced an existing construction loan. Built in 2025, Tenney North Park is an eight-story property located at 2260 El Cajon Blvd. It features 115 market-rate units and 10 affordable units, with studio, one-bedroom and two-bedroom floor plans averaging 727 square feet. The property also includes 3,116 square feet of ground-floor retail and three levels of parking totaling 146 spaces. Tenney North Park provides residents with proximity to North Park’s 30th Street dining and entertainment corridor, along with access to major employment and lifestyle destinations throughout San Diego, including Downtown San Diego, approximately 10 minutes away; the Hillcrest healthcare cluster, less than 10 minutes away; and UTC/La Jolla, approximately 20 minutes away. The post PCCP Provides $41M Refi on North Park Multifamily appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: PCCP provided $41M refi on 125-unit Tenney North Park, San Diego North Park submarket, built 2025.
115 market-rate + 10 affordable units; 8-story, mixed-use (3,116 sq ft retail); construction-to-permanent takeout.
Refinance of construction loan signals stable lease-up and lender confidence; proximity to employment hubs (Downtown 10 min, Hillcrest < 10 min).
stories.summary: PCCP provided a $41 million senior loan to refinance Tenney North Park, a newly constructed 125-unit multifamily property in San Diego's North Park submarket. Built in 2025 at 2260 El Cajon Blvd., the eight-story project includes 115 market-rate and 10 affordable units, ground-floor retail, and parking. The refinance converted an existing construction loan, reflecting stabilization post-lease-up.
stories.impact: Indicates strong lease-up fundamentals and lender appetite for market-rate multifamily in San Diego's North Park, a walkable, employment-adjacent urban submarket with proximity to Downtown and Hillcrest job centers. Successful construction-to-permanent takeout signals continued capital availability for similar urban infill projects in coastal California; however, no new supply or demand signal—this is a completion-stage event reflecting prior underwriting and development cycle.

stories.title: Pearlmark Provides $81M for Apartment Project in Coral Gables
stories.excerpt: Swiss investment firm Empira Group has secured an $81 million construction loan to build a 160-unit multifamily development in Coral Gables, Fla. Pearlmark provided the financing for Aurelian, a 12-story multifamily project on a 1.2-acre site at 114 Calabria Avenue. CBRE’s Charles Crapse and Denny St. Romain arranged the financing for Empira Group. The Business Journals first reported the financing. Empira acquired the property for $18 million in 2025, and recently broke ground on the development, which will include 248 parking spaces, a swimming pool, a fitness center, a yoga studio, coworking space, an entertainment lounge and a pet grooming station. Coral Gables-based Behar Font & Partners designed the building, which is expected to be completed in 2028. Empira also plans to add a 6,000-square-foot public park on the western portion of the property. The financing comes about 18 months after Empira secured $111.3 million to build an apartment tower in Miami’s Brickell Financial District. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Pearlmark provided $81M construction loan for 160-unit Aurelian in Coral Gables, Fla.; Empira Group (Swiss) developer.
12-story, $1.2-acre site at 114 Calabria Ave; broke ground recently; completion 2028; $18M land acquisition in 2025.
Amenities-rich (pool, fitness, yoga, coworking, pet grooming, 6,000-sf public park); appeals to affluent, urban workforce.
stories.summary: Swiss investment firm Empira Group secured an $81 million construction loan from Pearlmark to build Aurelian, a 160-unit multifamily development in Coral Gables, FL. The 12-story project, designed by Behar Font & Partners, acquired land for $18 million in 2025 and recently broke ground on a 1.2-acre site at 114 Calabria Ave. Expected completion is 2028, with amenities including 248 parking spaces, pool, fitness center, yoga studio, coworking, entertainment lounge, pet grooming, and a new 6,000-square-foot public park.
stories.impact: Signals foreign institutional capital actively deploying in South Florida multifamily, particularly in affluent Coral Gables. Empira's recent Brickell refi ($111.3M, 18 months prior) plus this new Coral Gables project shows sustained investor interest in premium urban Miami metros. Moderate construction cost and amenity intensity (coworking, pet services) reflect post-pandemic demand for lifestyle-integrated rentals. No signal of new employment anchor or population inflow, but continuous capital flow into Miami presumes ongoing demand; limited local impact on future development feasibility unless construction inflation moderates.

stories.title: Citi Provides $210M Refi for Grand Hyatt Resort in Southern California
stories.excerpt: Citi has provided $210 million in refinancing for Trinity Investments’ 531-key luxury hotel in Southern California’s Coachella Valley. JLL Capital Markets arranged the five-year, floating-rate, single-asset, single-borrower commercial mortgage-backed securities loan for the Grand Hyatt Indian Wells Resort & Villas. The financing comes after a $62 million renovation and conversion of the property to the Grand Hyatt brand in 2024. The 45-acre resort is at 44600 Indian Wells Lane in Indian Wells in Riverside County, about 20 miles southeast of Palm Springs. The property features 449 guestrooms, 39 suites and 43 villas, as well as more than 88,000 square feet of indoor and outdoor meeting and event space. The resort also includes nine swimming pools, a water park, a 30,000-square-foot spa, six restaurants and bars, and tennis and pickleball courts. Kevin Davis, Americas CEO of JLL’s hotels and hospitality group, said that recently renovated resorts are attracting more lenders. “The hospitality financing market has shown meaningful momentum this year, with lenders focusing capital on repositioned assets with institutional sponsorship in markets where supply constraints support sustained performance,” Davis said in a statement. JLL’s Mike Huth and Jade Lewin arranged the financing with Davis. Miami-based Trinity specializes in acquiring, repositioning and operating hotels and resorts, and has deployed more than $10 billion across the United States, Mexico, Europe and Japan. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Citi provided $210M refi (5-yr, floating-rate CMBS) for 531-key Grand Hyatt Resort, Coachella Valley, Riverside County.
Post-$62M renovation and 2024 conversion to Grand Hyatt brand; 45-acre resort, 20 miles SE of Palm Springs.
Hospitality/resort asset; no multifamily relevance.
stories.summary: Citi provided $210 million in refinancing for Trinity Investments' 531-key Grand Hyatt Indian Wells Resort & Villas in Riverside County, CA. The five-year, floating-rate, single-asset CMBS loan financed the property following a $62 million renovation and 2024 conversion to the Grand Hyatt brand. The 45-acre resort features 449 guestrooms, 39 suites, 43 villas, meeting and event space, pools, spa, and dining.
stories.impact: No impact on multifamily development. This is a luxury hospitality refi in the Coachella Valley, reflecting resort market recovery and lender confidence in recently branded/renovated properties, but does not inform apartment demand, supply, or cost in any residential metro.

stories.title: L.A. Industrial Vacancy Falls for First Time in Two Years
stories.excerpt: Los Angeles County’s industrial real estate market extended its recovery over the summer with its fourth quarter in a row of positive net absorption and its first annual decline in vacancy in at least two years. A new report from CBRE shows industrial tenants absorbed 1.9 million square feet during the third quarter, compared with negative 2.4 million square feet during the same period a year earlier. The market has had 5.1 million square feet of absorption since the start of the year, following more than two years of quarterly losses between mid-2023 and late 2025. The vacancy rate fell 20 basis points from both the second quarter and a year earlier to 5 percent, while leasing activity reached 13.7 million square feet, up 6.5 percent year-over-year. However, leasing volume declined 15.7 percent from the second quarter. Demand was particularly strong for larger warehouses. Industrial buildings measuring at least 250,000 square feet accounted for almost 2.1 million square feet of positive absorption during the third quarter. Those properties represented about 96 percent of the space absorbed this year. Smaller industrial properties have struggled, however. Buildings smaller than 50,000 square feet recorded negative absorption of 320,000 square feet during the quarter and 1.43 million square feet through September. Despite improving occupancy, average direct asking rents held steady at $1.19 per square foot per month on a triple-net basis, following declines in 10 of the previous 11 quarters. That figure remains 4 percent below the average from a year ago, and 30.4 percent below the $1.71 per square foot recorded in the third quarter of 2023. Central L.A. led the county with 1.11 million square feet of positive absorption, followed by the South Bay with 488,000 square feet and the San Gabriel Valley with 442,000 square feet. bullets: L.A. County industrial vacancy fell 20 bps to 5% in Q3; first annual decline in 2+ years; 1.9M sf positive absorption.
5.1M sf YTD absorption; large-format warehouses (250k+ sf) drove 2.1M sf Q3 absorption; leasing activity up 6.5% YoY.
Recovery from 2+ years of quarterly losses (mid-2023 to late 2025); Amazon and logistics tenants driving demand.
stories.summary: Los Angeles County's industrial market showed its first annual decline in vacancy in at least two years, with the vacancy rate falling 20 basis points to 5% in Q3. The market absorbed 1.9 million square feet in Q3 (versus negative 2.4M a year earlier) and 5.1M square feet YTD. Leasing activity reached 13.7 million square feet, up 6.5% year-over-year, with particularly strong demand for large-format warehouses (250k+ sf), which accounted for 2.1M sf of Q3 absorption.
stories.impact: Industrial recovery signals renewed logistics and e-commerce tenant demand across L.A. County, which indirectly supports multifamily demand in industrial submarkets (Inland Empire, Gateway, Vernon, Ontario area). Positive absorption and lower vacancy indicate landlord pricing power and capital deployment to industrial; however, this does not directly drive apartment demand or supply in L.A. multifamily submarkets unless tied to employment growth. No second-order effect on multifamily development unless industrial job growth (warehousing labor) is quantified in metro employment forecasts.

stories.title: Walker & Dunlop Investment Partners Supplies $63M Refi for Illinois Apartments
stories.excerpt: Noah Properties has landed $62.5 million of lease-up financing for a newly built multifamily development in suburban Chicago, Commercial Observer has learned. Walker & Dunlop Investment Partners (WDIP) originated the loan for 945 Nanusha Residences in Buffalo Grove, Ill. The deal refinances existing construction debt ahead of its temporary certificate of occupancy (TCO) , prior to the lease-up process. Arrow Real Estate Advisors negotiated the transaction with a team led by Morris Betesh and Jacob Petrovic. The refi was structured with an interest reserve through lease-up to finance remaining project costs and cover real estate tax and insurance expenses, according to Arrow. “WDIP stepped up on a pre-TCO takeout that materially reduces Noah’s cost of capital, carries the property all the way through stabilization on a single loan and closed in roughly 30 days from sign-up,” Petrovic, director at Arrow Real Estate Advisors, said in a statement. Betesh, founder and managing partner at Arrow, said Chicago and the Midwest have been “a core growth priority” for the brokerage this year, with 945 Nanusha Residences showcasing this conviction of “high-quality product in deep suburban submarkets.” Located at 945 North Old Arlington Heights Road around 30 miles northwest of Downtown Chicago, 945 Nanusha Residences consists of 223 apartments across 231,970 gross square feet. Resident amenities include a courtyard, a swimming pool, cabanas, an outdoor grilling area, a rooftop lounge with fire pit, a fitness center and electric vehicle charging stations. WDIP and Noah Properties did not immediately return requests for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Walker & Dunlop Investment Partners provided $62.5M lease-up refi for 945 Nanusha Residences, Buffalo Grove, IL (suburban Chicago).
Newly built multifamily; pre-TCO takeout with interest reserve through lease-up; ~30-day close time.
Noah Properties developer; refi reduced cost of capital and carried property through stabilization on single loan.
stories.summary: Noah Properties obtained $62.5 million in lease-up financing from Walker & Dunlop Investment Partners for 945 Nanusha Residences, a newly built multifamily development in Buffalo Grove, IL. The loan refinanced existing construction debt ahead of temporary certificate of occupancy and is structured with an interest reserve to finance remaining costs and cover taxes and insurance through lease-up and stabilization. Arrow Real Estate Advisors negotiated the transaction, which closed in approximately 30 days.
stories.impact: Indicates strong lender appetite for lease-up takeouts in suburban Chicago (North Shore/Buffalo Grove market), with competitive pre-TCO execution reducing developer capital costs and de-risking stabilization. Successful, rapid close suggests confidence in Chicago suburban multifamily fundamentals and lease-up velocity. For developers, this signals available lease-up financing capacity in Chicago metro; however, no new supply or demand signal—reflects completion-stage execution of existing pipeline.

stories.title: Skin Care Brand FaceGym to Open New Tribeca Location at 110 Reade Street
stories.excerpt: Time to face the music. FaceGym, a skin care brand that describes itself as a “facial fitness” studio, has inked a 10-year, 2,400-square-foot lease for a new Tribeca spot at 110 Reade Street, according to landlord broker Platinum Commercial. Founded in 2014 in London, FaceGym offers customers “facial workouts” and “combines muscle manipulation techniques” to provide lifting and sculpting services without surgery, according to its website. The brand has 15 locations globally, including four others in New York City on the Upper East Side, in NoHo and in Midtown. “The strongest retail brands today are making long-term investments in neighborhoods that complement their identity and where they can build lasting relationships with their customers,” Platinum Commercial’s Steven Evans, who repped landlord 110 Reade Property Owner LLC, said in a statement. “Tribeca has evolved into one of Manhattan’s premier destinations for luxury wellness, beauty and experiential retail, attracting brands that value authenticity, quality and community. FaceGym is an ideal addition to that ecosystem.” The asking rent was $110 per square foot. The new location is expected to open this month. Isaacs and Company represented the tenant, but the names of the brokers who represented the tenant were not immediately available. Built in 1861 near the corner of Reade Street and West Broadway, 110 Reade Street is a six-story, mixed-use residential property with ground-floor retail. Fitness studio Pure Barre was a former tenant in the retail space. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: FaceGym (London-founded wellness brand) signed 10-yr, 2,400-sf lease at 110 Reade Street, Tribeca, Manhattan.
Brand has 15 global locations, 4 other NYC spots (Upper East Side, NoHo, Midtown); 5th NYC location.
Retail/wellness tenant; no multifamily relevance.
stories.summary: FaceGym, a London-founded 'facial fitness' studio brand, signed a 10-year, 2,400-square-foot lease at 110 Reade Street in Tribeca. The brand, which offers facial workouts and muscle manipulation techniques, has 15 locations globally and four existing New York City locations. This Tribeca location is its fifth NYC site and reflects expansion in Manhattan's premium wellness and experiential retail markets.
stories.impact: No direct impact on multifamily development. This reflects Tribeca retail leasing activity and the neighborhood's evolution as a luxury wellness destination, but does not signal population demand, employment growth, or supply-side constraints affecting apartment development in Manhattan or outer boroughs.
